title: Runtime-aware model binding and routing shim for safe versioned rollouts
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Context: We need a robust mechanism to bind model versions to runtime versions at routing time that allows safe gradual rollouts across LTS/edge channels, supports automatic fallbacks, and provides clear observability for compatibility regressions. Current problem: model->runtime compatibility is expressed only in a static matrix and baked into the scheduler heuristics. This causes operational blast radius during model or runtime upgrades because there is no lightweight per-request compatibility check or graceful fallback shim. Goals:
- Provide a runtime-side middleware (routing shim) that evaluates a model/runtime compatibility score at request time and selects the best serving target while honoring explicit version pins and customer-specified policies (strict, preferred, flexible).
- Support LTS channels and ephemeral release channels: allow customers and internal rollouts to pin to channel names (e.g., runtime:lts-2025-10, model:stable, model:canary) rather than raw semver, with a mapping maintained by the control plane.
- Implement safe fallback policies: when a preferred pairing is unavailable or fails compatibility checks, route to the highest-compatible variant according to policy and emit a structured event for automatic rollback triggers.
- Ensure rollout gates: integrate gate checks (canary success rate, error budget, perf delta) before widening a route.
- Provide telemetry and controls for per-tenant rollbacks and emergency global failover to a golden model/runtime pair.
Acceptance criteria:
1) Routing shim implemented in the serving proxy that can: evaluate compatibility metadata, consult control-plane mapping, and select a target per request under three policies (strict, ideal, fallback).
2) Customers can pin to channels (LTS or release names) in API and console; control plane resolves channels to concrete versions.
3) Fallback behaviors: on compatibility mismatch or runtime error, request is retried once to a compatible fallback; if fallback used, event recorded and UI flagged.
4) Rollout gate API: rollout jobs can define success windows and gate thresholds; the system will automatically pause rollouts when gates fail and annotate the rollout record.
5) End-to-end tests covering matrix permutations (model major/minor deltas vs runtime patch levels), canary to 10%/50%/100% rollout steps, and simulated KV cache incompatibilities.
6) Documentation: control-plane docs + console UX spec + release notes and migration guide for ops.
Design summary:
- Compatibility metadata: models and runtimes will publish a small compatibility manifest with fields: supported_runtime_semver_range, kv_cache_format_version, recommended_kernel_flags, compatibility_score (0-100). These are stored in the model catalog and runtime registry.
- Runtime routing shim: lightweight component placed in the request path, performs: 1) resolve customer pin/channel via control-plane API, 2) fetch compatibility manifest for candidate model variants and local runtime version, 3) compute compatibility score and policy decision, 4) route or fallback and emit structured telemetry.
- Control-plane mapping: channel -> canonical version mapping stored in the control-plane DB with roll-forward rules for LTS (allow only patch updates) vs rolling (allow minor updates after gates).
- Rollout gates: implemented as a reusable gate engine used by both model and runtime rollout jobs. Gate signals pull from metrics (latency P95, error rate, quality checks from eval service).
Trade-offs and constraints:
- Runtime-side checks add ~0.6-1.5ms of latency; mitigations: local caching of manifest + compatibility heuristic + async refresh.
- Full semantic checks (e.g., KV cache bit-level) expensive to do per request; we only do an approximate compatibility score per request and background verification jobs for deep checks.
- Security: routing shim must honor tenant isolation and not leak manifests across tenants; manifests are per-tenant for private deployments.
